config.title: useDebounce

intro.title: useDebounce
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that uses a debounced function to delay API calls until the user stops typing. You will learn the core concept of debouncing, which helps optimize performance by preventing excessive function executions. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API with `ref` for reactive state and a custom `useDebounce` composable. This beginner-friendly project will teach you how to implement and apply debouncing in a real-world Vue application.
intro.usecase: Debouncing is essential in real-world Vue applications where user interactions trigger frequent updates. Search inputs in e-commerce sites like Amazon use debouncing to wait until users finish typing before fetching results, preventing excessive API calls. Dashboard filters for data visualization tools like Tableau apply debouncing when adjusting date ranges or metrics to avoid recalculating charts on every slider movement. Form validation in sign-up flows also benefits by delaying validation checks until users pause typing, creating smoother user experiences.

objectives: Implement a debounced search input using Vue's Composition API
Construct a custom useDebounce composable function
Initialize reactive state to manage debounced values
Configure the debounce delay parameter to control timing behavior
Bind the debounced value to display updated search results
Integrate the useDebounce composable into a Vue component
Manipulate the debounced value in response to user input events

steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a reactive state variable called searchInput using ref, initialized to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from 'vue' to create reactive state. For example: const searchInput = ref('')

// Creating reactive state with ref

successCriteria: searchInput is declared using ref with an initial value of empty string, and is returned from the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

// Similar: another reactive state variable

steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a second reactive state variable named debouncedSearch that will later hold the debounced version of the search input.
successCriteria: A debouncedSearch variable is declared using ref with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Define the debounce handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named debounceHandler that takes two parameters: callback and delay. The function should return a new function that will be the debounced version of the callback.
steps.hint: Create a function that returns another function. The inner function will handle the debounce logic using setTimeout.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a debounceHandler function defined in your setup function that can be used to create debounced versions of other functions.
successCriteria: The debounceHandler function is defined with parameters (callback, delay) and returns a new function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your debounceHandler function takes two parameters (callback and delay) and returns a new function. Check that you're using the correct syntax for defining functions in Vue's setup.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounceHandler function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named debounceHandler that accepts callback and delay parameters and returns another function. Look at the analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Create debounced update function using the handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named debouncedUpdate that uses the debounceHandler to update debouncedSearch with the current searchInput value after a 500ms delay.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls debounceHandler with a callback that sets debouncedSearch.value to searchInput.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The debouncedUpdate function is defined and ready to be called when searchInput changes.
successCriteria: A function named debouncedUpdate is defined that uses debounceHandler to update debouncedSearch with searchInput.value after 500ms.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your debouncedUpdate function calls debounceHandler with a callback that updates debouncedSearch.value with searchInput.value, and specifies 500ms as the delay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debouncedUpdate function isn't defined correctly. It should use debounceHandler to create a function that updates debouncedSearch with the current searchInput value after 500ms.

steps.title: Set up watcher for search input changes
steps.instruction: Add a watch call inside the setup function that watches the searchInput ref and calls the debouncedUpdate function whenever it changes.
steps.hint: Use the watch API imported earlier. The first argument should be searchInput, and the second argument should be the debouncedUpdate function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The watch will monitor searchInput changes and trigger the debouncedUpdate function, which will eventually update debouncedSearch after a delay.
successCriteria: A watch call is added that watches searchInput and calls debouncedUpdate when it changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling watch with searchInput as the first argument and debouncedUpdate as the second argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The watch wasn't set up correctly. Remember to use the watch function with searchInput as the reactive value to watch and debouncedUpdate as the callback.
